releases.title: Record over USB
notes: USB audio. Record the FM-1’s stereo mix in your DAW at 44.1 or 48 kHz (16-bit). The recording includes effects and any metronome clicks. Look for “CoralFlower In” or “CoralFlower FM-1” in your DAW’s audio settings. MIDI works over the same USB connection, and the analogue output stays on.

MIDI Clock In. When playback is stopped, MIDI Start plays the selected rhythm, pattern or song from the beginning. MIDI Stop halts playback, and MIDI Continue resumes from that point. If your DAW sends a song position while playback is stopped, the FM-1 can resume from there. After your DAW sends MIDI Stop, you can still play the arpeggiator from the FM-1’s keys. You can also play it if the external clock drops out during playback. The sequencer and rhythm hold their place, and the arpeggiator syncs again when the clock returns.

PLAY without an external clock. With CLOCK set to In and no external clock, press PLAY to start a rhythm or pattern at the FM-1’s own tempo. If the clock drops out during playback, press PLAY to stop, then press it again to restart. If there’s still no external clock, the FM-1 uses its own tempo.

Notes and drums under heavy load. When the FM-1 has to cut sounds, it looks for fading sounds to cut before considering held polyphonic notes. It now accounts for the attack of a clap in both the classic and X kits when deciding which sounds to cut.
USB fix. This update fixes a case where the firmware could get stuck after a USB controller timeout.

releases.title: Fixes for Undo and SEL
notes: After you copy a rhythm into a pattern, Undo now restores that pattern to its previous state and leaves other patterns unchanged.
While you hold “SEL” in a track editor, the message now updates when you change “BARS”, “POSITION”, or the selected drum. It shows what will be cleared when you let go.

releases.title: Newer FM-1 support and sequencer controls
notes: FM-1s with the newer UC25HQ80 chip can save sounds, settings and patterns across power-off and enter update mode from CoralFlower.
SELECT now picks patterns and SONG. ALGORITHM selects tracks and song blocks.
Copy a rhythm into a pattern with an empty Drums track. In DRUMS, hold and release SEL to clear the selected drum from its active bars.
Sound edits now survive power-off, including edits to a pattern’s own sounds.

releases.title: Every chord in the take
notes: A chord you play right after REC always goes into the take.
On the rhythm machine, REC counts one bar in, then the take and the rhythm start together.
Your patterns, sounds and settings stay as they are.

releases.title: 23 rhythms and six new kits
notes: A rhythm machine plays 23 ready-made rhythms under your chords, from Pop to Breakcore.
EDIT turns a rhythm into a pattern, and REC records your chords over it.
Six new drum kits play on CoralFlower's own drum engine, and IN CH picks your MIDI keyboard's channel.

releases.title: A sound for every pattern
notes: Each pattern can have its own sounds, and the song switches them block by block.
A HOLD key keeps your chord playing after you let go.
A MIDI keyboard can play the FM-1's keys, or play roots while you pick chord types.

releases.title: Everything as you left it
notes: Settings and sound edits are saved as you go and kept when you switch off.
PLAY picks up the pattern or song you picked last.
Fast chords on heavy FM sounds stay whole, right from power-on.

releases.title: Write while it plays
notes: The keys write chords into a pattern while it plays; hold EDIT and turn SELECT to move a chord.
Each pattern has its own mutes, and you can switch to the song while it plays.
The crash rings like metal, and a dimmed KEY or SCALE tells you why.

releases.title: REC records straight into the sequencer
notes: REC on the main screen records your chords into a new sequencer pattern; the looper is gone.
A loop you saved becomes a pattern the next time you switch on.
Your drum hits, the beats and the playing step light up on the keys.

releases.title: Patterns in the backup
notes: A backup now holds the sequencer's patterns and song, with your sounds, settings and loop.
Restore brings the patterns back. Backups made with 0.3 don't have them.
After an install, the page says where to make a backup.

releases.title: A sequencer for chords, bass and drums
notes: A sequencer: eight patterns and a song, each pattern with Chords, Bass, Layer and Drums tracks.
Eleven drums in eight kits you can mix, each drum with its own level.
An arpeggio or a strum can play a track, and single notes glide too.

releases.title: Whole chords strike again
notes: RETRIG has a new setting, Chord: the whole chord starts again, gliding from the last one.
Glide on VA sounds now takes the time you set.
The Lock layouts show a padlock in the top bar.

releases.title: The first release
notes: The lower keys play the notes of your scale; hold an upper key, and each note becomes a chord.
A bass part, an arpeggiator with a strum, a looper and about 60 VA and FM sounds.
A flower (Top layout) or a coral (Side layout) grows from every chord.
